title: How Robots Find the Shortest Path: A* Search in 60 Seconds 🗺️ #shorts
description:
A* (A-star) is the path-finding algorithm behind robots, games and maps. Each square gets a score f = g + h: g is the real distance travelled so far, h is a quick guess of the distance left (counting squares, ignoring walls). A* always explores the square with the lowest score, so it heads toward the goal instead of searching everywhere, and still finds the shortest path around obstacles.

lines: A robot needs to cross a room full of obstacles. Which way is the shortest?
A blind search spreads out in every direction, checking almost every square in the room.
A* is smarter. Every square gets a score: F equals G plus H. G is the distance travelled so far. H is a quick guess of the distance left, counting squares and ignoring walls.
It always explores the square with the lowest score next, so it pulls toward the goal, and bends around walls only when it has to.
When it reaches the goal, it traces back the cheapest route: the shortest path, after checking far fewer squares.
Distance so far, plus a smart guess. That's A*.
